name: Saint Joseph
description: Patron of workers, the universal Church, and fathers. Husband of the Blessed Virgin Mary and foster father of Jesus. A carpenter in Nazareth, he protected the Holy Family during their flight into Egypt and raised the Son of God with love and humility.
patronOf: Workers, fathers, families, the Church, dying people

name: Saint Patrick
description: Patron saint of Ireland, known for bringing Christianity to the Irish people in the 5th century. Born in Roman Britain, he was captured by Irish pirates and enslaved. After escaping, he returned as a bishop to evangelize Ireland.

name: Saint Francis of Assisi
description: Founder of the Franciscan Order, lover of poverty and nature. He received the stigmata — the wounds of Christ — in 1224. His Canticle of the Sun is one of the first known works of Italian literature.

name: Saint Teresa of Ávila
description: Doctor of the Church and mystic. She reformed the Carmelite Order and wrote profound spiritual classics including The Interior Castle and The Way of Perfection. Her teachings on contemplative prayer remain foundational.

name: Saint Anthony of Padua
description: Doctor of the Church, Franciscan friar, and one of the most beloved saints. Known for his powerful preaching and miraculous deeds. He is invoked for finding lost items and aiding the poor.
patronOf: Lost items, poor people, travelers, Portugal, Brazil

name: Saint Peter the Apostle
description: Chief of the Apostles, to whom Jesus gave the keys of the Kingdom of Heaven. First Bishop of Rome and first Pope. Martyred by crucifixion upside-down under Emperor Nero around 64–68 AD.

name: Saint Paul the Apostle
description: Apostle to the Gentiles, missionary, and author of much of the New Testament. Born Saul of Tarsus, he persecuted early Christians before his dramatic conversion on the road to Damascus. He traveled the Mediterranean world founding churches.

name: Saint Mary Magdalene
description: A devoted disciple of Jesus Christ. She was present at the crucifixion and burial of Jesus, and was the first to witness the Resurrection — earning her the title 'Apostle to the Apostles.'

name: Saint Augustine of Hippo
description: Doctor of the Church and philosopher. His autobiography Confessions is one of the greatest spiritual writings in history. He wrestled deeply with sin before his conversion, writing: 'Our heart is restless until it rests in You.'

name: Saint Thérèse of Lisieux
description: The 'Little Flower,' she entered Carmel at 15 and died of tuberculosis at 24. Her autobiography Story of a Soul introduced her 'little way' — doing small things with great love — which transformed Catholic spirituality worldwide.

name: Saint Nicholas
description: Bishop of Myra in the 4th century, known for his generosity to the poor. He secretly provided dowries for three impoverished sisters, throwing bags of gold through their window at night — a story that inspired the legend of Santa Claus.

name: Saint John the Baptist
description: Prophet and precursor of Jesus Christ. He baptized Jesus in the Jordan River, crying 'Behold the Lamb of God!' He was beheaded by Herod Antipas at the request of Salome.

name: Saint Catherine of Siena
description: Doctor of the Church, mystic, and political reformer. She successfully urged Pope Gregory XI to return the papacy to Rome from Avignon. Her spiritual masterwork The Dialogue remains a treasury of mystical theology.

name: Saint Ignatius of Loyola
description: Founder of the Society of Jesus (Jesuits). A Spanish soldier who underwent a spiritual conversion during recovery from battle wounds, he composed the Spiritual Exercises — a 30-day program of prayer still used worldwide.

name: Saint Dominic
description: Founder of the Order of Preachers (Dominicans) and promoter of the Rosary. He established a mendicant order dedicated to preaching and scholarship to combat heresy through truth rather than force.

name: Saint Clare of Assisi
description: Founder of the Order of Poor Ladies (Poor Clares). Inspired by Francis of Assisi, she embraced radical poverty. She is patroness of television because she reportedly witnessed the Christmas Mass on the wall of her cell when too ill to attend.

name: Saint John Paul II
description: Pope from 1978 to 2005, one of the most traveled and influential popes in history. He played a pivotal role in ending Communism in Poland. Authored numerous encyclicals and beatified and canonized more saints than any previous pope.

name: Saint Benedict of Nursia
description: Founder of Western monasticism and the Benedictine Order. His Rule of Saint Benedict — which calls monks to a life of ora et labora (pray and work) — became the foundation of monastic life in the Western Church.

name: Saint Luke the Evangelist
description: Physician, companion of Paul, and author of the third Gospel and the Acts of the Apostles. His Gospel emphasizes mercy, the Holy Spirit, prayer, and the role of women. Tradition holds he painted the first icon of the Virgin Mary.

name: Saint John the Evangelist
description: The 'beloved disciple' and youngest Apostle. Author of the fourth Gospel, three epistles, and the Book of Revelation. He stood at the foot of the Cross and was entrusted with the care of the Virgin Mary.

name: Saint Stephen
description: The first Christian martyr (protomartyr). One of the seven deacons chosen by the Apostles, he was stoned to death after delivering a powerful speech before the Sanhedrin. Saul of Tarsus (later Paul) witnessed his martyrdom.

name: Saint Valentine
description: A Roman priest and physician martyred in 269 AD. He is associated with love and courtly romance, though little historical detail is known. His feast day became linked to romantic love in 14th-century English poetry.
patronOf: Love, engaged couples, happy marriages, beekeepers

name: Saint Christopher
description: A giant of a man who carried a child across a river, only to discover the child was Christ carrying the weight of the world. His name means 'Christ-bearer.' Despite being removed from the general Roman calendar in 1969, he remains beloved.

name: Blessed Virgin Mary (Assumption)
description: The Assumption of Mary celebrates the dogma that Mary was assumed body and soul into heavenly glory. One of the most ancient feasts of the Church, it is celebrated with great solemnity as a holy day of obligation in most countries.

name: Saint Thomas Aquinas
description: Doctor of the Church and the greatest theologian of the Middle Ages. His masterwork Summa Theologiae synthesized Aristotelian philosophy with Christian theology and remains the foundation of Catholic intellectual tradition.

name: Saint Teresa of Calcutta
description: Founder of the Missionaries of Charity. She devoted her life to the poorest of the poor in Calcutta's slums. Her simple words — 'Not all of us can do great things. But we can do small things with great love' — echo worldwide.
patronOf: World Youth Day, missionaries of charity

name: Saint George
description: Soldier-martyr venerated since the 3rd century. The legend of slaying a dragon to rescue a princess symbolizes the triumph of good over evil and faith over fear. Patron of England, Georgia, and many other nations.

name: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary
description: Princess of Hungary who gave up royal life to care for the poor. Widowed at 20, she joined the Third Order of Saint Francis and spent her remaining years in service to the sick and destitute, dying at 24.

name: Saint Faustina Kowalska
description: Polish mystic and apostle of Divine Mercy. Her diary, Divine Mercy in My Soul, records visions of Jesus who asked her to spread the message of His mercy. The Divine Mercy devotion now reaches millions worldwide.

name: Archangel Michael
description: Chief among the angels, defender of the Church, and patron of soldiers. He leads the heavenly army in the defeat of Satan in the Book of Revelation. The Prayer to Saint Michael is said after Mass in many parishes.

name: Aziz Yusuf
description: İşçilerin, evrensel Kilise'nin ve babaların koruyucusu. Kutsal Bakire Meryem'in eşi ve İsa'nın manevi babası. Nasıra'da bir marangozdu; Kutsal Aile'yi Mısır'a kaçışları sırasında korudu ve Tanrı'nın Oğlu'nu sevgi ve alçakgönüllülükle büyüttü.
patronOf: İşçiler, babalar, aileler, Kilise, ölmekte olanlar

name: Aziz Patrick
description: İrlanda'nın koruyucu azizi, 5. yüzyılda Hristiyanlığı İrlanda halkına getirmesiyle tanınır. Roma Britanyası'nda doğdu, İrlandalı korsanlar tarafından esir alınıp köle edildi. Kaçtıktan sonra İrlanda'yı Hristiyanlaştırmak için piskopos olarak geri döndü.

name: Assisili Aziz Francis
description: Fransisken Tarikatı'nın kurucusu, yoksulluk ve doğa sevgisiyle tanınır. 1224'te Mesih'in yaralarını, yani stigmata'yı aldı. Güneş Ezgisi, İtalyan edebiyatının bilinen ilk eserlerinden biridir.

name: Avilalı Azize Teresa
description: Kilise Doktoru ve mistik. Karmelit Tarikatı'nı reforme etti ve İç Kale ile Kemal Yolu gibi derin ruhsal klasikler yazdı. Tefekkür duası üzerine öğretileri hâlâ temel niteliktedir.
patronOf: Baş ağrısı çekenler, İspanya, satranç oyuncuları

name: Padualı Aziz Anthony
description: Kilise Doktoru, Fransisken keşişi ve en sevilen azizlerden biri. Güçlü vaazları ve mucizevi işleriyle tanınır. Kayıp eşyaların bulunması ve yoksullara yardım için kendisine dua edilir.
patronOf: Kayıp eşyalar, yoksullar, yolcular, Portekiz, Brezilya

name: Havari Aziz Petrus
description: İsa'nın Göklerin Egemenliği'nin anahtarlarını verdiği Havarilerin başı. Roma'nın ilk Piskoposu ve ilk Papa. İmparator Nero döneminde, MS 64–68 civarında baş aşağı çarmıha gerilerek şehit edildi.

name: Havari Aziz Pavlus
description: Milletlere Havari, misyoner ve Yeni Ahit'in büyük bölümünün yazarı. Tarsuslu Saul olarak doğdu, Şam yolunda yaşadığı çarpıcı dönüşümden önce ilk Hristiyanlara zulmetti. Akdeniz dünyasını dolaşarak kiliseler kurdu.

name: Azize Meryem Magdalena
description: İsa Mesih'in sadık bir öğrencisi. İsa'nın çarmıha gerilişinde ve gömülüşünde hazır bulundu ve Dirilişe tanıklık eden ilk kişi oldu — bu ona 'Havarilerin Havarisi' unvanını kazandırdı.
patronOf: Tefekkür edenler, kadınlar, parfümcüler, din değiştirenler

name: Hippolu Aziz Augustinus
description: Kilise Doktoru ve filozof. Otobiyografisi İtiraflar, tarihin en büyük ruhsal eserlerinden biridir. Dönüşümünden önce günahla derin bir mücadele verdi ve şöyle yazdı: 'Yüreğimiz, Sende huzur bulana dek huzursuzdur.'

name: Lisieuxlu Azize Thérèse
description: 'Küçük Çiçek' olarak bilinir, 15 yaşında Karmel'e girdi ve 24 yaşında veremden öldü. Otobiyografisi Bir Ruhun Öyküsü, dünya çapında Katolik maneviyatını dönüştüren 'küçük yolunu' — küçük şeyleri büyük sevgiyle yapmayı — tanıttı.

name: Aziz Nikolaos
description: 4. yüzyılda Myra Piskoposu, yoksullara cömertliğiyle tanınır. Üç fakir kız kardeşe gizlice çeyiz sağladı, geceleyin pencerelerinden altın torbaları attı — bu hikaye Noel Baba efsanesine ilham verdi.

name: Vaftizci Yahya
description: İsa Mesih'in habercisi ve peygamberi. Şeria Nehri'nde İsa'yı vaftiz etti ve 'İşte Tanrı Kuzusu!' diye haykırdı. Salome'nin isteği üzerine Herod Antipas tarafından başı kesilerek şehit edildi.

name: Sienalı Azize Catherine
description: Kilise Doktoru, mistik ve siyasi reformcu. Papa XI. Gregorius'u papalığı Avignon'dan Roma'ya geri getirmeye ikna etmeyi başardı. Ruhsal başyapıtı Diyalog, mistik teolojinin bir hazinesi olmaya devam ediyor.

name: Loyolalı Aziz Ignatius
description: İsa Cemiyeti'nin (Cizvitler) kurucusu. Savaş yaralarından iyileşirken ruhsal bir dönüşüm yaşayan İspanyol bir askerdi; dünya çapında hâlâ kullanılan 30 günlük bir dua programı olan Ruhsal Alıştırmalar'ı kaleme aldı.

name: Aziz Dominic
description: Vaizler Tarikatı'nın (Dominikenler) kurucusu ve Tespih'in yaygınlaştırıcısı. Sapkınlığa karşı güç yerine gerçekle mücadele etmek için vaaz ve bilime adanmış bir dilenci tarikatı kurdu.

name: Assisili Azize Clare
description: Yoksul Hanımlar Tarikatı'nın (Clarisler) kurucusu. Assisili Francis'ten ilham alarak radikal yoksulluğu benimsedi. Hastalığı nedeniyle kiliseye gidemediğinde Noel Ayini'ni hücresinin duvarında gördüğü rivayet edildiğinden televizyonun koruyucu azizesidir.

name: II. Yuhanna Pavlus
description: 1978'den 2005'e kadar Papa'lık yaptı, tarihin en çok seyahat eden ve etkili papalarından biri. Polonya'da Komünizmin sona ermesinde kilit bir rol oynadı. Sayısız genelge yazdı ve önceki hiçbir papadan daha fazla azizi kutsadı ve azizlik ilan etti.

name: Nursialı Aziz Benedictus
description: Batı manastırcılığının ve Benediktin Tarikatı'nın kurucusu. Keşişleri ora et labora (dua et ve çalış) yaşamına çağıran Aziz Benedictus Kuralı, Batı Kilisesi'nde manastır yaşamının temeli oldu.

name: İncilci Aziz Luka
description: Hekim, Pavlus'un yol arkadaşı, üçüncü İncil'in ve Elçilerin İşleri'nin yazarı. İncili merhameti, Kutsal Ruh'u, duayı ve kadınların rolünü vurgular. Geleneğe göre Bakire Meryem'in ilk ikonasını o resmetti.

name: İncilci Aziz Yuhanna
description: 'Sevgili öğrenci' ve en genç Havari. Dördüncü İncil'in, üç mektubun ve Vahiy Kitabı'nın yazarı. Çarmıhın dibinde durdu ve Bakire Meryem'in bakımıyla görevlendirildi.

name: Aziz İstefanos
description: İlk Hristiyan şehidi (protomartir). Havariler tarafından seçilen yedi diyakozdan biri, Sanhedrin önünde güçlü bir konuşma yaptıktan sonra taşlanarak öldürüldü. Tarsuslu Saul (sonradan Pavlus) şehadetine tanık oldu.

name: Aziz Valentinus
description: MS 269'da şehit edilen Romalı bir rahip ve hekim. Aşk ve romantizmle ilişkilendirilir, ancak tarihsel ayrıntısı azdır. Bayram günü, 14. yüzyıl İngiliz şiirinde romantik aşkla bağlantılı hale geldi.
patronOf: Aşk, nişanlı çiftler, mutlu evlilikler, arıcılar

name: Aziz Christophoros
description: Bir çocuğu nehirden taşıyan dev cüsseli bir adam; sonradan çocuğun dünyanın ağırlığını taşıyan Mesih olduğunu keşfetti. Adı 'Mesih taşıyıcısı' anlamına gelir. 1969'da genel Roma takviminden çıkarılmasına rağmen hâlâ sevilir.

name: Kutsal Bakire Meryem (Göğe Alınış)
description: Meryem'in Göğe Alınışı, Meryem'in beden ve ruhuyla göksel görkeme alındığı dogmasını kutlar. Kilise'nin en eski bayramlarından biridir; çoğu ülkede zorunlu bir bayram olarak büyük görkemle kutlanır.

name: Aziz Thomas Aquinas
description: Kilise Doktoru ve Orta Çağ'ın en büyük ilahiyatçısı. Başyapıtı Summa Theologiae, Aristoteles felsefesini Hristiyan teolojisiyle birleştirdi ve Katolik entelektüel geleneğinin temeli olmaya devam ediyor.

name: Kalkütalı Azize Teresa
description: Sevgi Misyonerleri'nin kurucusu. Hayatını Kalküta'nın gecekondularındaki en yoksullara adadı. Sade sözleri — 'Hepimiz büyük şeyler yapamayız. Ama küçük şeyleri büyük sevgiyle yapabiliriz.' — dünya çapında yankılanmaya devam ediyor.

name: Aziz Georgios
description: 3. yüzyıldan beri saygı gösterilen asker-şehit. Bir prensesi kurtarmak için ejderha öldürme efsanesi, iyinin kötüye ve imanın korkuya karşı zaferini simgeler. İngiltere, Gürcistan ve birçok başka ulusun koruyucusudur.

name: Macaristanlı Azize Elizabeth
description: Yoksullara bakmak için kraliyet hayatından vazgeçen Macaristan Prensesi. 20 yaşında dul kaldı, Aziz Francis'in Üçüncü Tarikatı'na katıldı ve kalan yıllarını hastalara ve yoksullara hizmet ederek geçirdi, 24 yaşında öldü.

name: Azize Faustina Kowalska
description: Polonyalı mistik ve İlahi Merhamet'in havarisi. Günlüğü, Ruhumda İlahi Merhamet, kendisinden merhametinin mesajını yaymasını isteyen İsa'nın görümlerini kaydeder. İlahi Merhamet ibadeti bugün dünya çapında milyonlara ulaşıyor.

name: Başmelek Mikail
description: Meleklerin başı, Kilise'nin savunucusu ve askerlerin koruyucusu. Vahiy Kitabı'nda Şeytan'ın yenilgisinde göksel orduya öncülük eder. Aziz Mikail Duası birçok cemaatte Ayin sonrasında okunur.

name: Saint Jude Thaddeus
description: Apostle of Jesus Christ, traditionally identified as the brother of Saint James the Less and a relative of Jesus. He is the author of the Epistle of Jude and is believed to have preached the Gospel in Judea, Samaria, Idumaea, Syria, Mesopotamia, and Libya, dying as a martyr.

name: Saint Rita of Cascia
description: Augustinian nun known as the 'Saint of the Impossible.' Widowed after a difficult marriage and the death of her sons, she entered the Augustinian convent at Cascia, Italy. She received a wound on her forehead resembling a thorn from the Crown of Thorns, which remained with her until her death.
patronOf: Impossible causes, difficult marriages, widows, abuse victims

name: Saint Maximilian Kolbe
description: Polish Franciscan friar who volunteered to die in place of a stranger, a husband and father, at Auschwitz concentration camp in 1941. He was canonized by Pope John Paul II in 1982 as a martyr of charity. Before his imprisonment he founded a Franciscan community devoted to Mary Immaculate.
patronOf: Journalists, families, prisoners, the pro-life movement

name: Saint Pio of Pietrelcina (Padre Pio)
description: Italian Capuchin priest and mystic who bore the stigmata — the visible wounds of Christ's Passion — for fifty years. Known for his long hours hearing confessions and gift of spiritual discernment, he founded the 'Home for the Relief of Suffering' hospital. He was canonized by Pope John Paul II in 2002.
patronOf: Confessors, civil defense volunteers, adolescents, stress relief

name: Saint John Vianney
description: French parish priest known as the Curé of Ars, celebrated for his extraordinary zeal in the confessional, where he spent up to sixteen hours a day hearing confessions. Despite early struggles with his studies, he became renowned for holiness, penance, and pastoral care of souls. Canonized by Pope Pius XI in 1925.

name: Saint Bernadette Soubirous
description: A poor miller's daughter from Lourdes, France, who in 1858 reported eighteen apparitions of the Blessed Virgin Mary at the Grotto of Massabielle. She later became a Sister of Charity at Nevers, embracing a hidden life of humility and suffering until her death. Canonized by Pope Pius XI in 1933.

name: Saint Kateri Tekakwitha
description: A Mohawk-Algonquin laywoman born in 1656 in present-day New York, she converted to Catholicism as a teenager despite persecution from her family and village, and took a vow of perpetual virginity. Known as the 'Lily of the Mohawks,' she is the first Native American to be canonized, by Pope Benedict XVI in 2012.

name: Saint Carlo Acutis
description: Italian teenager known for his deep devotion to the Holy Eucharist and his skill with computers, which he used to build a website cataloguing Eucharistic miracles around the world. He died of leukemia in 2006 at age fifteen, offering his sufferings for the Church. Beatified in 2020 and canonized by Pope Leo XIV in 2025.

name: Saint Cecilia
description: Roman virgin martyr of the early Church, traditionally said to have heard heavenly music in her heart on her wedding day and to have consecrated her virginity to God. She was martyred for her faith and is one of the most venerated of the early Roman martyrs.

name: Saint Lucy
description: Virgin martyr of Syracuse, Sicily, who died during the persecution of Diocletian in the early 4th century. She consecrated her virginity to God and distributed her dowry to the poor before being betrayed and put to death. Her name, meaning 'light,' has long linked her to prayers for eyesight.

name: Saint Monica
description: Mother of Saint Augustine of Hippo, she endured a difficult marriage and prayed with tears for seventeen years for her son's conversion, which finally came through the preaching of Saint Ambrose in Milan. She died at Ostia shortly after witnessing Augustine's baptism.
patronOf: Mothers, wives, victims of abuse, patience

name: Saint Jerome
description: Doctor of the Church renowned for translating the Old and New Testaments into Latin, producing the Vulgate at the invitation of Pope Damasus I. A scholar and ascetic with a famously sharp temperament, he spent his final decades in a cave near Bethlehem devoted to study and prayer.

name: Saint Rose of Lima
description: Peruvian mystic and member of the Dominican Third Order, she was the first person born in the Americas to be canonized. She lived a life of great penance and prayer while caring for the sick, the poor, and the elderly in her native Lima.

name: Saint Vincent de Paul
description: French priest known as the 'Apostle of Charity,' who devoted his life to serving the poor and sick. He founded the Congregation of the Mission and, together with Saint Louise de Marillac, the Daughters of Charity. He was canonized in 1737.

name: Saint Gianna Beretta Molla
description: Italian pediatrician, wife, and mother who chose to continue a dangerous pregnancy rather than undergo treatment that would have saved her life at the cost of her unborn child. She died in 1962, a week after giving birth to her daughter. She was canonized by Pope John Paul II in 2004.

name: Saint Martin de Porres
description: Peruvian Dominican lay brother of mixed African and Spanish descent, born in Lima in 1579. Despite the racial prejudice of his era, he became renowned for his humility, healing gifts, and tireless care of the sick, poor, and enslaved. He was canonized by Pope John XXIII in 1962.
patronOf: Mixed-race people, barbers, public health workers, social justice

name: Saint Josephine Bakhita
description: Sudanese woman kidnapped and sold into slavery as a child, who gained her freedom in Italy and entered the Canossian Daughters of Charity. Known for her serenity and forgiveness toward her former captors, she spent decades in humble service to her community. She was canonized by Pope John Paul II in 2000.
patronOf: Sudan, victims of human trafficking, kidnapping survivors

name: Saint Pier Giorgio Frassati
description: Italian layman known for his cheerful faith, love of mountain climbing, and tireless service to the poor of Turin. A member of the Third Order of Saint Dominic, he died of polio in 1925 at age 24, likely contracted while caring for the sick. He was canonized by Pope Leo XIV in 2025.
patronOf: Young people, mountaineers, World Youth Day

name: Saint John Bosco
description: Italian priest and founder of the Salesians of Don Bosco, who devoted his life to the education and care of poor and abandoned boys in Turin. Known as the 'Father and Teacher of Youth,' he combined faith, reason, and kindness in his approach to forming young people. He was canonized by Pope Pius XI in 1934.

name: Saint Elizabeth Ann Seton
description: The first person born in the United States to be canonized a saint. Widowed with five children, she converted to Catholicism, founded the Sisters of Charity of St. Joseph, and opened the first free Catholic school for girls in America at Emmitsburg, Maryland. She was canonized by Pope Paul VI in 1975.

name: Saint Maria Goretti
description: Italian girl martyred in 1902 at age eleven while resisting a sexual assault; she forgave her attacker before dying of her wounds, and he later repented after seeing her in a vision. She was canonized by Pope Pius XII in 1950, with her mother present at the ceremony.

name: Saint Francis Xavier
description: Spanish Jesuit priest and co-founder of the Society of Jesus alongside Saint Ignatius of Loyola. He undertook extensive missionary journeys through India, Southeast Asia, and Japan, baptizing thousands, and died in 1552 on an island off the coast of China while awaiting entry to the mainland. He was canonized by Pope Gregory XV in 1622.

name: Saint Philip Neri
description: Italian priest known as the 'Apostle of Rome,' celebrated for his cheerful holiness, humor, and tireless work hearing confessions. He founded the Congregation of the Oratory to foster prayer, preaching, and community among laypeople and clergy. He was canonized by Pope Gregory XV in 1622.

name: Saint Anne
description: Mother of the Blessed Virgin Mary and grandmother of Jesus Christ. According to ancient Christian tradition, she and her husband Joachim were an elderly, childless couple who conceived Mary after years of fervent prayer. She is venerated as a model of faithful motherhood and is especially honored in Quebec and Brittany.
patronOf: Mothers, grandmothers, housewives, women in labor, Quebec

name: Saint Agnes of Rome
description: A young Roman virgin martyred around 304 AD during the persecution of Diocletian, traditionally said to have been only twelve or thirteen years old when she was killed for refusing to renounce her consecration to Christ. She is one of seven women commemorated by name in the Roman Canon of the Mass.
patronOf: Virgins, chastity, young girls, rape victims, gardeners

name: Saint Frances Xavier Cabrini
description: Italian-born religious sister who emigrated to the United States in 1889 at the request of Pope Leo XIII to serve Italian immigrants. She founded the Missionary Sisters of the Sacred Heart of Jesus and established dozens of schools, hospitals, and orphanages across the Americas and Europe. She became a naturalized U.S. citizen and was the first American citizen to be canonized, by Pope Pius XII in 1946.

name: Saint John of the Cross
description: Spanish Carmelite friar, mystic, and Doctor of the Church. Together with Saint Teresa of Ávila, he reformed the Carmelite Order and founded the Discalced Carmelites. Imprisoned and persecuted by friars opposed to the reform, he composed his celebrated mystical poem 'Dark Night of the Soul' during his captivity.

name: Saint Damien of Molokai
description: Belgian priest of the Congregation of the Sacred Hearts who volunteered to serve the leprosy patients exiled to the Kalaupapa settlement on the island of Molokai, Hawaii. He lived among them for sixteen years, building homes, a church, and a hospital, before contracting leprosy himself and dying in 1889. He was canonized by Pope Benedict XVI in 2009.
patronOf: Lepers, outcasts, Hawaii, people with HIV/AIDS

name: Saint Andrew the Apostle
description: Brother of Saint Peter and a fisherman from Bethsaida, he was a disciple of John the Baptist before becoming the first of the Twelve to be called by Jesus, earning him the title 'Protoclete' ('first-called'). Tradition holds he preached in Greece and Asia Minor and was martyred at Patras, bound to an X-shaped cross now known as the Saint Andrew's Cross.

name: Saint Thomas the Apostle
description: One of the Twelve Apostles, remembered as 'Doubting Thomas' for refusing to believe in the Resurrection until he could touch Christ's wounds, after which he professed 'My Lord and my God.' Tradition holds he carried the Gospel to India, where the Saint Thomas Christians of Kerala trace their origin to his mission, and that he was martyred there.

name: Saint Bartholomew the Apostle
description: One of the Twelve Apostles, often identified with Nathanael, whom Jesus described as 'an Israelite indeed, in whom there is no guile.' Tradition holds he preached the Gospel in Armenia and was martyred by being flayed alive, which is why he is depicted in art holding his own skin.

name: Saint Matthew the Apostle
description: A tax collector who was sitting at his customs post when Jesus called him with the words 'Follow me,' after which he left everything to become one of the Twelve Apostles. He is traditionally credited as the author of the Gospel of Matthew.

name: Saint James the Greater
description: Son of Zebedee and brother of Saint John the Evangelist, he was a fisherman called by Jesus alongside his brother. One of the inner circle of three Apostles present at the Transfiguration and the Agony in the Garden, he was the first of the Twelve to be martyred, beheaded by Herod Agrippa I around 44 AD. His shrine at Santiago de Compostela became one of Christendom's great pilgrimage sites.

name: Saint Barnabas
description: A Levite from Cyprus originally named Joseph, he was renamed 'Barnabas' ('son of encouragement') by the Apostles after selling his property and giving the proceeds to the early Church. He introduced the newly converted Saul of Tarsus to the Apostles and accompanied him on his first missionary journey. Though not one of the Twelve, he is honored with the title of Apostle.

name: Saint John Chrysostom
description: Doctor of the Church and Archbishop of Constantinople, renowned for his eloquent preaching that earned him the surname 'Chrysostom' ('Golden-mouthed'). His homilies on Scripture and his reforming zeal for the poor angered the imperial court, leading to his exile, where he died in 407. The Divine Liturgy of Saint John Chrysostom remains the principal liturgy of the Byzantine Rite.

name: Saint Ambrose
description: Doctor of the Church and Bishop of Milan, a former Roman governor chosen by popular acclaim to lead the see while still an unbaptized catechumen. A gifted preacher and hymn writer, he instructed and baptized Saint Augustine and firmly opposed both Arianism and imperial overreach into Church affairs. He died in 397.

name: Saint Basil the Great
description: Doctor of the Church and Bishop of Caesarea in Cappadocia, one of the great Cappadocian Fathers who defended the Nicene faith against Arianism. He wrote a monastic rule that shaped Eastern monasticism, founded a complex of charitable institutions for the poor and sick, and is honored jointly with Saint Gregory Nazianzen on this feast.

name: Saint Blaise
description: A bishop and physician in Armenia martyred under the persecution of Licinius in the early 4th century. Tradition holds he miraculously saved a boy from choking on a fishbone, giving rise to the blessing of throats performed in his name on his feast day with crossed candles.

name: Saint Sebastian
description: A Roman soldier martyred under Emperor Diocletian for his Christian faith. Condemned to be shot with arrows and left for dead, he was nursed back to health by Saint Irene of Rome, but returned to confront the emperor and was then clubbed to death. He is among the most frequently depicted saints in Christian art.

name: Saint Joan of Arc
description: French peasant girl who, guided by visions of saints, led the French army to victory during the Hundred Years' War before being captured and burned at the stake in 1431. Retried and exonerated in 1456, she was canonized by Pope Benedict XV in 1920.

name: Saint Isidore the Farmer
description: Spanish farm laborer of Madrid renowned for his piety, charity to the poor, and devotion to daily Mass even amid his work in the fields. Tradition holds that angels were seen plowing beside him. He was canonized in 1622 together with Saints Ignatius of Loyola, Francis Xavier, Teresa of Ávila, and Philip Neri.

name: Saint Alphonsus Liguori
description: Italian bishop, moral theologian, and founder of the Redemptorists (Congregation of the Most Holy Redeemer), devoted to preaching missions among the rural poor. His prolific writings on moral theology emphasized mercy over rigorism. He was declared a Doctor of the Church in 1871.

name: Saint Francis de Sales
description: Bishop of Geneva and Doctor of the Church known as the 'Gentleman Saint' for his gentle, patient approach to guiding souls. With Saint Jane Frances de Chantal he founded the Order of the Visitation, and his classic Introduction to the Devout Life brought a spirituality of holiness in everyday life to ordinary lay people. He was declared patron of writers and journalists by Pope Pius XI in 1923.
patronOf: Writers, journalists, the Catholic press, educators

name: Saint John of God
description: Portuguese-born founder of the Order of Hospitallers (Brothers Hospitallers of Saint John of God). After a dramatic religious conversion in Granada, Spain, he devoted the rest of his life to caring for the sick, the poor, and the homeless, opening a hospital that became the model for his religious order. He was canonized in 1690 by Pope Alexander VIII.
patronOf: Hospitals, nurses, the sick, booksellers, printers

name: Saint Bridget of Sweden
description: Swedish mystic, wife, and mother of eight children, including Saint Catherine of Sweden. After her husband's death she founded the Bridgettine Order (Order of the Most Holy Savior) and recorded her mystical visions in her Revelations. She was canonized in 1391 and declared a co-patroness of Europe by Pope John Paul II in 1999.

name: Saint Ignatius of Antioch
description: Apostolic Father and third Bishop of Antioch, traditionally held to be a disciple of the Apostle John. Condemned under Emperor Trajan, he was taken to Rome to be martyred by wild beasts in the Colosseum, and along the journey wrote seven epistles to Christian communities that are among the earliest and most treasured documents of the early Church.

name: Saint Polycarp
description: Bishop of Smyrna and disciple of the Apostle John, he was one of the Apostolic Fathers linking the age of the Apostles to the great Church Fathers who followed. When ordered during a public persecution to curse Christ and be spared, he refused, saying he had served Christ for eighty-six years and would not deny Him now; he was burned at the stake around the year 155.

name: Saint Edith Stein (Teresa Benedicta of the Cross)
description: German Jewish philosopher and student of Edmund Husserl who converted to Catholicism in 1922 and became a Discalced Carmelite nun, taking the name Teresa Benedicta of the Cross. Arrested by the Nazis in 1942 in reprisal for the Dutch bishops' public condemnation of anti-Semitism, she died in the gas chambers at Auschwitz. She was canonized by Pope John Paul II in 1998 and named a co-patroness of Europe.

name: Blessed Miguel Pro
description: Mexican Jesuit priest who ministered secretly to the faithful during the anti-Catholic persecution of the Cristero War, disguising himself to celebrate Mass and administer the sacraments despite the risk of death. Arrested on a false charge, he was executed by firing squad in 1927 without trial, reportedly extending his arms in the form of a cross and crying out '¡Viva Cristo Rey!' before he died. He was beatified by Pope John Paul II in 1988.

name: Saint John Henry Newman
description: English theologian and Oxford academic who led the Oxford Movement within Anglicanism before being received into the Catholic Church in 1845, after which he founded the Birmingham Oratory. A cardinal and one of the most influential Catholic thinkers of the modern era, he wrote extensively on conscience and doctrine, including his autobiography Apologia Pro Vita Sua. He was canonized by Pope Francis in 2019.

name: Saint Katharine Drexel
description: American heiress who renounced her fortune to found the Sisters of the Blessed Sacrament for Indians and Colored People, dedicating her life and inheritance to establishing missions and schools for Native American and African American communities across the United States. She founded Xavier University of Louisiana, the first Catholic university in the U.S. for African Americans. She was canonized by Pope John Paul II in 2000.

name: Saint André Bessette (Brother André)
description: Canadian lay brother of the Congregation of Holy Cross known for his deep devotion to Saint Joseph and his humble ministry as a doorkeeper at Notre Dame College in Montreal, where he became renowned for reported healings attributed to his prayers. He founded Saint Joseph's Oratory of Mount Royal, now one of the largest shrines to Saint Joseph in the world. He was canonized by Pope Benedict XVI in 2010.

name: Saint Athanasius of Alexandria
description: Doctor of the Church and Bishop of Alexandria, the chief defender of Nicene orthodoxy against the Arian heresy in the 4th century. He was driven from his see into exile five times by Arian emperors and bishops for his unwavering insistence that Christ is fully divine and consubstantial with the Father, spending more than seventeen years away from Alexandria in total. He authored 'On the Incarnation' and the Life of Saint Anthony, and is honored as one of the four great Doctors of the Eastern Church in both the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox traditions.

name: Saint Seraphim of Sarov
description: Russian Orthodox monk, hermit, and spiritual elder (starets) of Sarov Monastery, born Prokhor Moshnin in Kursk, Russia, in the mid-18th century. He lived for years in solitude in the forest before returning to guide the many pilgrims who sought him out, teaching that the goal of the Christian life is 'the acquisition of the Holy Spirit.' He died in 1833 and was canonized by the Russian Orthodox Church in 1903. As a saint venerated primarily in Eastern Orthodoxy, his feast is kept on January 2, the date of his repose on the Orthodox liturgical calendar, rather than on the Roman General Calendar.

name: Saint Anthony the Great
description: Egyptian Desert Father regarded as the father of Christian monasticism. Around the age of twenty he gave away his inheritance and withdrew into the desert to pursue a life of prayer and asceticism, later organizing his many followers into a loosely knit monastic community. Saint Athanasius's Life of Antony spread his example across the Christian world, and he is especially venerated as a founding father by the Coptic Orthodox Church, whose monastery bearing his name in the Eastern Desert of Egypt remains an active spiritual center.
patronOf: Monks, gravediggers, basket weavers, skin diseases

name: Saint Nektarios of Aegina
description: Greek Orthodox bishop, theologian, and wonder-worker who served as Metropolitan of Pentapolis before enduring unjust accusations and removal from office, which he bore with humility and without complaint. He later founded the Holy Trinity Monastery on the island of Aegina, where he spent his final years in prayer, writing, and spiritual direction. Widely venerated for miracles of healing, especially among those suffering from cancer, he was glorified as a saint by the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople in 1961. As a saint of the Eastern Orthodox Church, his feast is kept on the Orthodox liturgical calendar rather than on the Roman General Calendar.

name: Saint Silouan the Athonite
description: Russian Orthodox monk of the Saint Panteleimon Monastery on Mount Athos, born Semyon Antonov in Tambov province. After years of intense spiritual struggle he received an assurance from Christ that shaped his teaching ever after: 'Keep thy mind in hell, and despair not.' His conversations and writings, preserved by his disciple Archimandrite Sophrony, became influential texts of modern Orthodox spirituality. He was glorified as a saint by the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople in 1987. As a saint of the Eastern Orthodox Church, his feast is kept on the Orthodox liturgical calendar rather than on the Roman General Calendar.

name: Saint Gregory the Great
description: Pope from 590 to 604 and Doctor of the Church, counted among the four great Doctors of the Western Church alongside Augustine, Ambrose, and Jerome. He reformed the Roman liturgy and chant — later known as Gregorian Chant — sent Saint Augustine of Canterbury to evangelize England, and wrote extensively on pastoral care and the Scriptures, taking for himself the title 'Servant of the Servants of God.'

name: Saint Irenaeus of Lyons
description: Bishop of Lyon in the 2nd century and a disciple of Saint Polycarp, who had himself been taught by the Apostle John. His chief work, Against Heresies, offered a systematic refutation of Gnosticism and a defense of apostolic tradition, making him one of the first great Christian theologians. Pope Francis declared him a Doctor of the Church in 2022, giving him the title 'Doctor of Unity' for his witness to the common faith shared by the Churches of East and West.

name: Saint Thomas More
description: English lawyer, scholar, and statesman who served as Lord Chancellor under King Henry VIII. Renowned for his integrity, wit, and his treatise Utopia, he was imprisoned in the Tower of London and beheaded in 1535 for refusing to acknowledge the king as supreme head of the Church in England, declaring himself 'the king's good servant, but God's first.' He was canonized by Pope Pius XI in 1935 and is honored, together with Saint John Fisher, among the English Reformation martyrs.

name: Saint John of Damascus
description: Eastern monk, priest, and theologian of the 8th century, born in Damascus into a prominent Christian family serving the Umayyad court before he withdrew to the monastery of Saint Sabas near Jerusalem. He is remembered as the great defender of the veneration of icons during the Iconoclast controversy, and his work 'An Exact Exposition of the Orthodox Faith' summarized the theology of the Greek Fathers for centuries to come. He is honored as a Doctor of the Church in the Roman Catholic tradition and as one of the great Church Fathers in Eastern Orthodoxy.

name: Saint Mark the Evangelist
description: Author of the second Gospel, traditionally identified with the John Mark of the Acts of the Apostles who accompanied Saint Paul and Saint Barnabas and later assisted Saint Peter in Rome. Ancient tradition holds that he founded the Church of Alexandria in Egypt, and he is venerated as the founder and first Patriarch of the Coptic Orthodox Church. His relics are enshrined at St. Mark's Basilica in Venice, where he is honored as patron.
patronOf: Egypt, Venice, notaries, the Coptic Orthodox Church

name: Saint Gregory Nazianzen
description: Archbishop of Constantinople and Doctor of the Church, honored jointly with Saint Basil the Great on this feast in the Roman Catholic calendar. One of the three Cappadocian Fathers, he is called 'the Theologian' for his profound defense of the divinity of Christ and the Holy Spirit against Arianism at the First Council of Constantinople in 381. In the Eastern Orthodox Church he is venerated as one of the Three Holy Hierarchs, together with Saint Basil the Great and Saint John Chrysostom.

name: Saint Ephrem the Syrian
description: Syriac deacon, poet, and Doctor of the Church, known as the 'Harp of the Holy Spirit' for the hundreds of hymns he composed defending Nicene orthodoxy against Arian and Gnostic teaching. He served the church of Nisibis and later Edessa, living an ascetic life devoted to teaching, charitable relief during famine, and sacred poetry. He was declared a Doctor of the Church by Pope Benedict XV in 1920 and is also highly venerated throughout the Eastern and Oriental Orthodox Churches.
patronOf: Spiritual directors, spiritual leaders, Syriac Christians

name: Saint Bernard of Clairvaux
description: French Cistercian abbot and Doctor of the Church, called the 'Mellifluous Doctor' for the eloquence of his preaching and writing. He founded the Abbey of Clairvaux and became the leading force behind the rapid growth of the Cistercian order, while his sermons on the Song of Songs and his devotion to the Virgin Mary shaped medieval spirituality. He was declared a Doctor of the Church by Pope Pius VIII in 1830.

name: Saint Anselm of Canterbury
description: Italian-born Benedictine monk and Archbishop of Canterbury, regarded as the father of Scholasticism. In his Proslogion he formulated the celebrated 'ontological argument' for the existence of God, and in Cur Deus Homo he developed an influential account of the Atonement. He was declared a Doctor of the Church by Pope Clement XI in 1720.

name: Saint Hildegard of Bingen
description: German Benedictine abbess, mystic, composer, and polymath of the 12th century. She recorded her visions in the illuminated work Scivias, composed liturgical music still performed today, and wrote extensively on natural history and medicine. Pope Benedict XVI declared her a Doctor of the Church in 2012, making her one of only a handful of women to hold that title.

name: Saint Cyril of Jerusalem
description: Bishop of Jerusalem and Doctor of the Church in the 4th century, best remembered for his Catechetical Lectures, a series of instructions delivered to those preparing for baptism that remain a key witness to early Christian liturgy and doctrine. He endured repeated exiles amid the Arian controversies of his time before his teaching was vindicated at the First Council of Constantinople. He was declared a Doctor of the Church by Pope Leo XIII in 1883.

name: Martin Luther
description: German Augustinian friar and theologian whose 1517 Ninety-Five Theses challenging the sale of indulgences sparked the Protestant Reformation. He translated the Bible into German, wrote the Small Catechism and Large Catechism, and composed numerous hymns including 'A Mighty Fortress Is Our God.' He died in Eisleben, Germany, on February 18, 1546. He is not canonized a saint and is not invoked for intercession, but Lutheran churches and some other Western calendars commemorate him annually on the date of his death as a renewer of the Church and teacher of the faith.
patronOf: Commemorated by Lutheran churches as a reformer and teacher of the faith
